names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 20 iunie, «Sfântul Ierarh Calist, Patriarhul Constantinopolului»; the form is the bare name, the rest of the line being rank and see.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 20 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Κάλλιστος Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 20. јун ст. ст., „Свети Калист I, патријарх цариградски“ — Свети is not a rank and „патријарх цариградски“ is the rank and the see, and §6 takes both off. **The numeral is kept**, being part of what the heading itself prints of his name and the thing that tells him from the `callistus-ii-of-constantinople` the corpus also keeps. Both forms were measured: `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Калист I» and also for the bare «Калист», so **neither would have folded** and the numeral was kept on the heading’s own authority rather than to avoid a fold — the 19 June case again, where a by-name was kept with the fold clear either way.

death.note: Two books state a year of death and they disagree, so the field is widened rather than chosen. doxologia’s life: «Sfântul Patriarh Calist s-a stins din viață în anul 1363 în Serbia». The Охридски пролог for 20. јун ст. ст.: „Упокојио се 1368. године на путу за Серез“ — he reposed in the year 1368 on the road to Serres. saint.gr states no year of death, ending his second patriarchate «from 22 June 1354 until 1364» and saying he died unexpectedly at Serres; a tenure’s end is not a stated year of death, so 1364 is not one of the two readings the display names, and it falls inside this field in any case. Nothing is averaged and no book is preferred (5 October 2026).

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 20 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and it closes by saying the Church appointed his memory for 20 Ιουνίου. It is the patriarch Callistus I, monk of Iviron and hesychast, disciple of Gregory of Sinai, not the corpus's `callistus-angelikoudes`, whom saint.gr does not name on this day. The page's parenthesis «(; - 1364)» and its dating of his second patriarchate to 20 June 1364 disagree with the 1363 the folder's `dates` carries out of doxologia.ro; both are reported and neither is changed here.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 03.07.2026 (20. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети Калист I, патријарх цариградски“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 20 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **THREE BOOKS, THREE YEARS, AND THE FIELD IS WIDENED ACROSS TWO OF THEM.** The folder held `death` 1363 to 1363, display «1363», off doxologia’s life, «Sfântul Patriarh Calist s-a stins din viață în anul 1363 în Serbia». This book: „Упокојио се 1368. године на путу за Серез“ — he reposed in the year 1368 on the road to Serres. `death` earliest 1363, latest 1368, display **«1363 or 1368»**, basis traditional, both sentences in the note. **WHY saint.gr’S 1364 IS NOT IN THE DISPLAY AND IS NOT LOST EITHER.** That page ends his second patriarchate «from 22 June 1354 until 1364» and then says he died unexpectedly at Serres. **A tenure’s end is not a stated year of death**, so it is not one of the two readings the display names; and it falls inside the widened interval anyway, so nothing is excluded by leaving it out. The display names the two years two books state flatly as the year he died. Nothing is averaged, nothing is preferred, and **the five years are not split**. TWO BOOKS NOW AGREE ON THE PLACE, WHERE ONE HAD ONLY THE COUNTRY. doxologia said he died «în Serbia»; saint.gr said he died unexpectedly **at Serres**; this book has him die „на путу за Серез“, on the road to Serres. The agreement is on the town and the disagreement is only whether he reached it, and both are written. THE ERRAND, AND THE SERBIAN RULER’S NAME, WHICH TWO BOOKS GIVE DIFFERENTLY. „куда је ходио царици српској Јелени, да иште помоћ против Турака“ — he was going to the Serbian empress Jelena, to ask help against the Turks. doxologia had him there as the emperor’s ambassador and named no one; saint.gr has the Athonite delegations beg **Elizabeth** for his body and calls her the Serbian ruler who would not be moved. Two books, two names for the same woman at the same place, and **no folder holds either**: `ls saints | grep -iE 'jelena|helena'` returns nobody. No identification is made and no row. The errand itself — help against the Turks — is new. TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS AT MAGOULA, AND A SECOND PLACE FOR THE HOUSE OF SAINT MAMAS. „подвизавао се на Атону у скиту Магулу код Филотејског манастира пуних двадесет осам година“ — twenty-eight full years at the skete of Magoula **by the monastery of Philotheou**, a count and a neighbour neither other book gives. Then „Ту је он саградио доцније обитељ светог Маманта“ — **there** he later built the house of Saint Mamas, where doxologia put that house at **Tenedos**. Two books, two places for one foundation, both written and neither chosen. **No row for any Mamas folder**, of which the corpus keeps six: a dedication is not a relation, and an identification off a dedication’s name is not an identification. THE FOUR YEARS, REFUSED AS A DURATION. „Буде изабран за патријарха цариградског 1350. године. После четири године удаљи се с престола“ — elected in 1350 and after **four years** withdrawn. The 1350 agrees with both other books; the four years is a **duration**, which the standing rule refuses as a date, and it is written in no field. It also disagrees with saint.gr, which has him enthroned 10 June 1350 and resigning 27 November 1353 — three and a half years — which is a second reason not to write it and no reason to choose. WHAT HE WROTE, AND THE ONE NAME IN IT THAT HAS A FOLDER AND STILL TAKES NO ROW. „У друштву са Игњатијем саставио красно руководство за подвижнике. Осим тога написао житије светог Григорија Синаита и светог Теодосија Трновског, као и многобројне беседе“ — with Ignatius he composed a fine guide for ascetics, and besides that wrote the life of Gregory of Sinai and the life of Theodosius of Tarnovo, and many homilies. The Ignatius agrees with the folder’s older prose, which names «his good friend Ignatius of Xanthopouloi» and the eighth volume of the Philokalia; **no folder holds that man**, the nineteen `ignatius-*` folders being other men, so no row. **`theodosius-of-tarnovo` exists and takes no row**: the subject of a man’s scholarship is not his companion, which is the ruling the Russian 16 ноября batch paid for, and his name is written **here and not in the prose**, because «Theodosius of Tarnovo» is that folder’s display name exactly and §6’s trap is a display-name match. `gregory-of-sinai` is already `related` in both directions and the folder’s older prose already says he wrote his teacher’s life, so that row is not touched. **THE PROPHECY OF HIS DEATH, AND WHY ITS PROPHET TAKES NO ROW AND NO MENTION.** „Интересантно је споменути, како је свети Максим Капсокаливит прорекао смрт патријарху Калисту. На путу за Србију Калист удари на Свету Гору. Видећи га, свети Максим рече: ‹Овај старац неће више видети своје пастве, јер позади њега чује се надгробно пјеније: блажени непорочни в пути›“ — Maximus of Kapsokalyvia foretold the patriarch’s death: coming up to the Holy Mountain on his way to Serbia he was seen by Maximus, who said that this elder would not see his flock again, for behind him was heard the funeral chant, «Blessed are the undefiled in the way». `maximus-of-kapsokalyvia` exists. **It takes no row**, on the standing rule that the object of a wonder is not its subject: Callistus is the man prophesied over, not the prophet, and a prophecy spoken over a man passing through is not a kinship, however real the meeting. **This is the day’s identity question and it is the author’s to overturn** — unlike an appearance, which the Three Hierarchs ruling settled, the two men here were both alive and in one place, and if that is a relation the remedy is two `related_add` lines and a sentence in each life. **AND THE NAME IS KEPT OUT OF THE PROSE FOR A SECOND, MEASURED REASON**: `maximus-the-confessor`’s `display_name` is the bare string **«Maximus»**, measured on the corpus and not guessed, so even the forename alone would have tripped `related-floor` in both directions. The scene is in the life without either name, which is §6’s fix applied **before** `npm test` rather than after it, as 19 June had to. `types` UNTOUCHED, `office` UNTOUCHED. Свети is not a rank and „патријарх цариградски“ is the rank and the see: `patriarch` is on the folder and the `office` is already «Patriarch of Constantinople». „старац“ in the quotation is a form of address and not a type. No `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S FIFTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Свети Левкије, епископ врунтисиопољски, у Италији“ — Leucius, born in Alexandria, early into a monastery, counted worthy of great revelations and of a mighty grace, so that he raised the dead and drove demons out of men; bishop first in Alexandria, then by a command from heaven crossing into Italy to the pagan city of Vruntisiopolj, which he baptised whole and in which he built a church of the Mother of God; and after much and successful labour passing over into eternity in the time of the emperor Theodosius II, in the fifth century. **Three folders hold the name and not one of them is he.** `ls saints | grep -i leuci` returns exactly three: `leucius-of-caesarea`, a martyr of 249–251 kept with Thyrsus and Coronatus, who is not a bishop and not of Italy; `leucius-companion-of-peter`, a martyr kept with Peter and Severus on the Greek 11 January; and `leucius-of-volokolamsk`, a Russian. `ls saints | grep -iE 'brundis|brindis'` returns nobody at all. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written on this day, and no folder from me — and **the fifth century, Theodosius II and the city are written nowhere**, because there is nothing to write them on. The day’s verse is his, and a verse is not a hymn and not a folder either. THE DAY’S SIXTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Блажени Студије“ — Studius, a notable patrician and consul in Constantinople, who founded near the Golden Gate the church of Saint John the Forerunner and the monastery called the Studion after him; a house that became famous for many glorious men, spiritual fathers, ascetics and sufferers for the faith; destroyed by the Latin crusaders in 1204, restored by the emperor Constantine Palaeologus Porphyrogenitus in 1293, and with a Turkish mosque standing on the place now. `ls saints | grep -i studi` returns five folders and **every one of them is a Studite and not the Studius the house is named after** — `damascene-the-studite`, `james-of-studion`, `naucratius-the-studite`, `nicholas-the-studite`, `theodore-the-studite`. The last of those is the man this entry names as the house’s most famous son, and **he takes no row and no mention in any prose written today**: a founder’s monastery is a dedication and a later inhabitant of it is not a relation. Ruling 3 on Studius himself: named here, no folder from me, and **1204, 1293 and the consulship are written nowhere**. The Блажени of his heading therefore decides nothing, there being no folder for it to decide a type on; had there been one it would still be the §5 reading «fool-for-christ *or* righteous — read which», and a patrician and consul who founds a monastery is neither obviously.

hymns.text: Βασιλίδος ἐδείχθης Πατριάρχης θεόσοφος, καὶ ̔Αγίου ῎Ορους τὸ κλέος, τῶν Σεῤῥαίων θησαύρισμα, τῶν θείων δὲ Χριστοῦ ἡσυχαστῶν ὁ φίλος καὶ συνήγορος ὁμοῦ· διὸ πάντες πάτερ Κάλλιστε ἐν χαρᾷ ὑμνοῦμέν σε κραυγάζοντες· Δόξα τῷ σὲ δοξάσαντι Χριστῷ, δόξα τῷ σὲ θαυμαστώσαντι, δόξα τῷ χορηγοῦντι διὰ σοῦ ἡμῖν τὰ κάλλιστα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, ῏Ηχος αʹ, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the only apolytikion on the page of «Όσιος Κάλλιστος Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης», and it names him, the Holy Mountain and Serres

english.text: You were shown a God-wise patriarch of the Queen of cities, the boast of the Holy Mountain and the treasure of the people of Serres, at once the friend and the advocate of Christ's divine hesychasts. Therefore, father Callistus, we all hymn you in gladness and cry: glory to Christ who glorified you, glory to him who made you wonderful, glory to him who through you supplies us with what is best.
